---
title: "Independent schools"
subtitle: "What the published data say about England's independent schools, and how far a fair comparison with the state sector can go."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
X <- readRDS(here::here("data", "independent.rds"))
sc <- X$sector_counts
k <- function(s, col) X$ks4_cov[[col]][X$ks4_cov$sector == s]
al <- function(s, col) X$alev_sum[[col]][X$alev_sum$sector5 == s]
rt <- X$reduced_test
bk <- function(kind, col) X$by_kind[[col]][X$by_kind$kind == kind]
kc <- function(s) X$k45_cor$r[X$k45_cor$sector == s]
SEC_COL <- c("Independent" = DPURPLE, "State-funded mainstream" = BLUE, "State school sixth forms" = BLUE, "Colleges" = GREY)
n0 <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
tb <- function(t, k) if (k %in% names(t)) unname(t[[k]]) else 0
```

::: {.callout-important}
## In short

- **There is no value added at 16 for independent schools, and one cannot
  fairly be built from published data.** The two things that matter most
  in Value Added v2.1 are each school's prior attainment and its
  disadvantage. Neither is published for independent schools, and nor is
  absence.
- **Their published GCSE results are not comparable either.** Many
  independent schools enter IGCSEs that do not count in the performance
  tables, so their Attainment 8 is often far below what their pupils
  achieve.
- **One comparison does exist: value added at A level.** DfE publishes
  16-18 A level value added, from each student's GCSE results, for
  `r al("Independent", "schools")` independent schools on the same basis as
  state sixth forms. It is the fair comparison available now, with caveats
  of its own.
:::

## The sector {#sec-sector}

England has `r n0(sc$all_independent)` open independent schools. This page
is about the `r n0(sc$schools)` mainstream independent schools that teach
secondary ages, with about `r n0(round(sc$pupils, -3))` pupils of all ages
between them. The 2024/25 performance tables list
`r n0(k("Independent", "schools"))` independent schools with pupils at the
end of key stage 4 (a few have since closed or changed):
`r n0(k("Independent", "pupils"))` pupils, against
`r n0(k("State-funded mainstream", "pupils"))` in state-funded mainstream
schools, about `r round(100 * k("Independent", "pupils") / (k("Independent", "pupils") + k("State-funded mainstream", "pupils")))`%
of the cohort. Independent special schools are a different sector and are
left out.

- **Inspection:** `r tb(sc$inspectorate, "ISI")` are inspected by the
  Independent Schools Inspectorate (members of the associations) and
  `r tb(sc$inspectorate, "Ofsted")` by Ofsted.
- **Admissions:** `r tb(sc$admissions, "Selective")` say they are selective,
  `r tb(sc$admissions, "Non-selective")` non-selective, and
  `r tb(sc$admissions, "Not applicable")` give no policy.
- **Single-sex:** `r tb(sc$sex, "Girls")` girls' schools and
  `r tb(sc$sex, "Boys")` boys' schools.
- **Boarding:** `r tb(sc$boarding, "Has boarders")` have boarders.

```{r}
#| label: fig-map
#| fig-cap: "Mainstream independent schools teaching secondary ages (GIAS, June 2026), coloured by A level value added 2024/25 (DfE, grades per entry; purple above zero, green below; grey, none published). Circle size by number of pupils."
al_va <- X$alev |> filter(sector5 == "Independent") |> select(URN, va_alev, alev_n, va_alev_3)
mp <- X$sector |> filter(!is.na(lat)) |> left_join(al_va, by = "URN") |>
  left_join(X$ks4 |> filter(sector == "Independent") |> select(URN, att8, tpup), by = "URN")
pal <- leaflet::colorNumeric(c("#1b7837", "#a6dba0", "#f7f7f7", "#c2a5cf", "#762a83"), domain = c(-1, 1), na.color = "#bdbac8")
mp$col <- ifelse(is.na(mp$va_alev), "#bdbac8", pal(pmax(pmin(mp$va_alev, 1), -1)))
mp$tip <- paste0("<b>", htmltools::htmlEscape(mp$name), "</b><br>", htmltools::htmlEscape(mp$la),
  "<br>", ifelse(is.na(mp$pupils_gias), "", paste0(mp$pupils_gias, " pupils · ")), mp$sex, " · ", mp$inspectorate,
  "<br>Admissions: ", coalesce(mp$admissions, "not given"),
  "<br>Attainment 8 2024/25: ", ifelse(is.na(mp$att8), "not published", mp$att8),
  "<br>A level value added 2024/25: ", ifelse(is.na(mp$va_alev), "not published", sprintf("%+.2f", mp$va_alev)))
leaflet::leaflet(height = 520, options = leaflet::leafletOptions(scrollWheelZoom = FALSE)) |>
  leaflet::addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") |>
  leaflet::setView(-1.6, 52.8, 6) |>
  leaflet::addCircleMarkers(lng = mp$lon, lat = mp$lat, radius = 2.5 + sqrt(pmax(coalesce(mp$pupils_gias, 100), 0)) / 9,
    fillColor = mp$col, fillOpacity = 0.9, color = "#4a4560", weight = 0.6, label = lapply(mp$tip, htmltools::HTML)) |>
  leaflet::addLegend("bottomright", colors = c("#762a83", "#c2a5cf", "#f7f7f7", "#a6dba0", "#1b7837", "#bdbac8"),
    labels = c("+1 grade or more", "+0.5", "0", "−0.5", "−1 or less", "None published"),
    title = "A level value added", opacity = 0.9)
```

## What is published {#sec-data}

Value Added v2.1 sets each school's results against what its intake and
setting would predict. This is what exists for independent schools, term by
term:

| In the v2.1 model | State-funded schools | Independent schools |
|---|---|---|
| **Outcome:** Attainment 8 | Published | Published for `r round(100 * k("Independent", "att8_pub"))`%, but IGCSEs and other unapproved qualifications score nothing (@sec-att8) |
| Prior attainment (KS2) | Published | **None.** Many pupils never sat KS2 tests, and none is published |
| Disadvantage (FSM6) | Published | **None.** Fee-paying schools have no free school meals measure |
| Absence | Published | **None.** Independent schools are not in the absence collection |
| English as an additional language | Published | **None.** Not collected in the independent schools census |
| Pupil mobility | Published | **None** |
| SEN support and EHC plans | Published | **Published** (median SEN support `r pp(X$sen_cov$sen_sup[X$sen_cov$indep])`%, EHC plans `r pp(X$sen_cov$ehcp[X$sen_cov$indep])`%, against `r pp(X$sen_cov$sen_sup[!X$sen_cov$indep])`% and `r pp(X$sen_cov$ehcp[!X$sen_cov$indep])`% in state secondaries) |
| Neighbourhood education | Built from where pupils live | Only where the school is. Pupils travel further, and some board |
| Admissions, single-sex, sixth form | Published | Published (GIAS), though many give no admissions policy |
| Ethnicity, young carers | Published | **None** |

The January 2026 school census publishes headcounts by age and sex, and
boarders, for every independent school. It publishes none of the
measures of who the pupils are: free school meals, first language,
ethnicity and young carers are all blank. The only measures of need are
SEN support and EHC plans. Independent schools identify more SEN support
than state schools, mostly specific learning difficulties, and have far
fewer EHC plans.

## The Attainment 8 problem {#sec-att8}

```{r}
#| label: fig-att8
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8 per pupil, 2024/25 (performance tables, provisional): state-funded mainstream schools and independent mainstream schools with a published figure."
#| fig-height: 3.6
a8 <- X$ks4 |> filter(!is.na(att8))
ggplot(a8, aes(att8, fill = sector, colour = sector)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8, adjust = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SEC_COL, name = NULL) + scale_colour_manual(values = SEC_COL, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8 per pupil", y = NULL) + theme_note() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

Independent schools, nearly all fee-paying and many selective, would be
expected to have results well above the state average. Their published
Attainment 8 has a median of `r pp(k("Independent", "att8_med"))`, below
the state median of `r pp(k("State-funded mainstream", "att8_med"))`, and
`r round(100 * k("Independent", "under20"))`% of independent schools score
under 20. That does not reflect what their pupils achieve. Since 2017 the performance
tables count only approved qualifications, and many independent schools
enter their pupils for international GCSEs (IGCSEs), which are not on the
list. A pupil with a string of top IGCSE grades can score next to nothing.

The same schools' A level results show it:

```{r}
#| label: fig-k45
#| fig-cap: "Attainment 8 (2024/25) against A level average point score per entry (2024/25), schools with at least ten A level students. Dashed lines: the state-school bottom quarter on Attainment 8 and median on A levels."
#| fig-height: 4.4
k45 <- X$k45 |> mutate(sector = factor(sector, c("State-funded mainstream", "Independent")))
ggplot(k45, aes(att8, alev_aps, colour = sector)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = X$st_q1, linetype = "dashed", colour = GREY) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = X$st_aps_med, linetype = "dashed", colour = GREY) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ sector) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SEC_COL, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Attainment 8 per pupil (KS4)", y = "A level points per entry") + theme_note()
```

In state schools, a school's Attainment 8 and its A level results go
together (correlation `r pp(kc("State-funded mainstream"), 2)`). In
independent schools they are unrelated (`r pp(kc("Independent"), 2)`).
`r X$k45_flag$mismatch` of the `r X$k45_flag$n` independent schools with
both (`r round(100 * X$k45_flag$share)`%) are in the bottom quarter of state
schools on Attainment 8 and above the state median at A level. Published
Attainment 8 cannot be used to compare an independent school with anyone,
and from the published data we cannot tell which schools' figures are
complete.

## Could a reduced model stand in? {#sec-reduced}

If the missing terms cannot be had, one could fit a model on only what
independent schools do report (their neighbourhood, SEN, size, sex,
selection, sixth form, region and setting) and compare results with that.
We can test this where the answer is known: on state schools, against the
full v2.1 model.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reduced
#| tbl-cap: "A reduced model (only what independent schools report) against the full v2.1 specification, state-funded mainstream schools, 2024/25."
tibble(` ` = c("Variation in results explained (R²)", "Correlation of the reduced model's value added with v2.1's",
               "Schools put in the same fifth of value added", "Of the reduced model's top fifth, also in v2.1's top fifth"),
       `Full v2.1` = c(sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rt$r2_full), "1", "", ""),
       `Reduced` = c(sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rt$r2_reduced), sprintf("%.2f", rt$r_resid),
                     sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rt$same_fifth), sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rt$top_fifth_kept))) |>
  kt(align = "lrr")
```

Even among state schools, where the full data exist to check it against,
the reduced model gets value added badly wrong. It puts only
`r round(100 * rt$same_fifth)`% of schools in the right fifth. It does not
fail at random: without a measure of disadvantage it credits schools for
their intake.

```{r}
#| label: fig-kind
#| fig-cap: "Average value added (%) by kind of state school, 2024/25: the full v2.1 model and the reduced model. Grammar schools are left out: selection is in both models as a flag."
#| fig-height: 3
bkd <- X$by_kind |> tidyr::pivot_longer(c(full, reduced), names_to = "model", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(model = ifelse(model == "full", "Full v2.1", "Reduced (what independent schools report)"),
         kind = factor(kind, rev(c("Least disadvantaged fifth (FSM6)", "Single-sex", "Other non-selective", "Most disadvantaged fifth (FSM6)"))))
ggplot(bkd, aes(pct, kind, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.65) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", pct), hjust = ifelse(pct >= 0, -0.15, 1.15)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 3.2, colour = INK) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Full v2.1" = DPURPLE, "Reduced (what independent schools report)" = MPURPLE), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Average value added (% of Attainment 8)", y = NULL) + theme_note() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

The least disadvantaged fifth of state schools have value added of
`r sgn(bk("Least disadvantaged fifth (FSM6)", "full"), 1)`% on the full
model and `r sgn(bk("Least disadvantaged fifth (FSM6)", "reduced"), 1)`% on
the reduced one: the reduced model mistakes an advantaged intake for good
teaching. Independent schools' intakes are more advantaged than any state
school's, and selected by fees and often by entrance exam. A reduced model
would credit them with that advantage, by more than it does the most
advantaged state schools, and there is no published measure to correct it.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-drop
#| tbl-cap: "What each missing term costs: the full v2.1 specification fitted on state schools, 2024/25, with one term left out at a time."
X$drop_one |> transmute(`Left out` = term, `R²` = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * r2),
                        `Correlation of value added with the full model` = sprintf("%.2f", r_va)) |>
  kt(align = "lrr")
```

Each of the missing terms costs something on its own; together, as the
reduced model shows, they cost most of the measure.

## The comparison that exists: A level value added {#sec-alevel}

DfE publishes value added at 16-18 for every school and college with A
level students, independent schools included. It sets each student's A
level grades against those of students nationally with the same GCSE
results, and averages by school, in grades per A level entry. Because it
starts from each student's own prior results, it allows for the largest
thing the KS4 comparison cannot.

```{r}
#| label: fig-alevel
#| fig-cap: "A level value added, 2024/25 (DfE 16-18 performance tables, grades per entry), by kind of provider."
#| fig-height: 3.4
alv <- X$alev |> filter(!is.na(va_alev)) |>
  mutate(sector5 = factor(sector5, c("Colleges", "State school sixth forms", "Independent")))
ggplot(alv, aes(va_alev, fill = sector5, colour = sector5)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GREY) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.25, linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SEC_COL, name = NULL) + scale_colour_manual(values = SEC_COL, name = NULL) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.5, 1.5)) +
  labs(x = "A level value added (grades per entry)", y = NULL) + theme_note() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-alevel
#| tbl-cap: "A level value added by kind of provider, 2024/25. 'Above' and 'below': the 95% interval excludes zero (A level qualification value added)."
X$alev_sum |> mutate(s = factor(sector5, c("Independent", "State school sixth forms", "Colleges"))) |> arrange(s) |>
  transmute(Provider = sector5, `With a value added` = n0(schools), `A level students` = n0(students),
            `Median (grades per entry)` = sprintf("%+.2f", va_med),
            `Middle half` = sprintf("%+.2f to %+.2f", va_q1, va_q3),
            `A level points per entry (median)` = pp(aps_med, 1),
            `Clearly above zero` = paste0(round(100 * sig_up), "%"), `Clearly below` = paste0(round(100 * sig_dn), "%")) |>
  kt(align = "lrrrrrrr")
```

On this measure the typical independent school adds
`r sgn(al("Independent", "va_med"), 2)` of a grade per A level
entry, against `r sgn(al("State school sixth forms", "va_med"), 2)`
in state school sixth forms. `r round(100 * al("Independent", "sig_up"))`%
of independent schools are clearly above zero, against
`r round(100 * al("State school sixth forms", "sig_up"))`% of state sixth
forms. The spread within each sector is wider than the gap between them:
many state sixth forms do better than the typical independent school.

What it does and does not allow for:

- **Prior attainment, yes**: each student's GCSE results. How fully
  independent pupils' IGCSEs count in that baseline is set out in DfE's
  16-18 technical guidance, and is the first thing to check before leaning
  on the comparison.
- **Disadvantage, no.** DfE's 16-18 value added has no adjustment for
  disadvantage or context. At GCSE the v2.1 model finds disadvantage worth
  a good deal even after prior attainment, so some of the independent
  schools' lead is likely to be their intake rather than their teaching.
- **Who stays on, no.** Sixth forms choose their students and students
  choose sixth forms. The two sectors' A level cohorts are selected
  differently.
- **One year is noisy.** Three-year averages are published alongside, and
  are steadier.

## Is a comparison possible? {#sec-verdict}

| Comparison | Possible? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Value added at 16 on the v2.1 basis | **No** | No prior attainment, disadvantage or absence for independent schools, and an incomplete outcome |
| Raw GCSE results (Attainment 8) | **No** | IGCSEs and other unapproved qualifications score nothing, and which schools are affected cannot be told from the data |
| A reduced contextual model at 16 | **Not credibly** | It can be computed, but in the state sector it gets value added badly wrong and credits advantaged intakes; independent intakes are the most advantaged of all |
| A level value added (16-18) | **Yes, with caveats** | Published by DfE for `r al("Independent", "schools")` independent schools on the same basis as state sixth forms; allows for prior attainment, not disadvantage or selection into the sixth form |
| A level results, raw | Descriptive only | Comparable qualifications, but no allowance for intake |

### What would make a fair comparison at 16 possible

All of these are about what is published, not about any individual
pupil's records:

1. **Count what independent pupils sit.** Publish Attainment 8 with IGCSEs
   and other GCSE-equivalent certificates included, beside the official
   figure, so the outcome is complete.
2. **A starting point.** A prior-attainment measure for independent
   schools' pupils at entry, whether KS2 or an agreed baseline.
3. **Who the pupils are.** Some measure of disadvantage: bursary and
   fee-remission rates are the nearest equivalent to free school meals.
   First language, at least, as for state schools.
4. **Attendance.** Absence is the largest school-level term in v2.1, and
   independent schools are outside the collection.

Until then, the honest comparison is at A level, and it is a comparison
of what sixth forms add to students who arrive with the same GCSEs, not of
schools.

## Sources {#sec-sources}

- Get Information about Schools (GIAS), all establishments, June 2026.
- DfE, [Schools, pupils and their characteristics](https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/find-statistics/school-pupils-and-their-characteristics),
  January 2026, school-level data.
- DfE, [Special educational needs in England](https://explore-education-statistics.service.gov.uk/find-statistics/special-educational-needs-in-england),
  January 2026, school-level data.
- DfE, [Compare school and college performance](https://www.compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk/download-data):
  KS4 (provisional) and 16-18 (A level value added and results) 2024/25.
